question: The Kailasa Temple built in the 8th century is in which of the following state?
solution: The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Kailasa Temple**, also known as the **Ellora Cave 16**, is located in the **Ellora Caves** complex in the **Aurangabad district of Maharashtra**, India. • It was constructed in the **8th century** during the reign of the **Rashtrakuta dynasty**, under the patronage of King **Krishna I**. • The temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and represents Mount Kailash, the abode of Lord Shiva, as per Hindu mythology. • The Kailasa Temple is a monolithic rock-cut structure, meaning it was carved out of a single piece of rock from the top down, showcasing the advanced engineering and artistic skills of ancient Indian craftsmen. • The temple features intricate carvings, sculptures, and architectural designs, including depictions of Hindu deities, mythological stories, and elaborate pillared halls, making it one of the finest examples of Indian rock-cut architecture.
